items.text: Before comparing tracks, set expectations correctly.
There is no single "travel scientist" job in India.
If a page promises one, it is selling a fantasy, not a career map.
These come up constantly in "travel science career" searches, and they deserve an honest, direct answer rather than being quietly left out.

India's Antarctic and Arctic research programme, run through the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), sends a genuinely small number of scientists a year , almost always PhD-level specialists in glaciology, atmospheric science, or polar oceanography, to stations like Maitri and Bharati.
Test-range science, flight-test and trial-campaign work at DRDO, ISRO, or HAL, involves real travel to test sites like Chandipur, Sriharikota, or Thumba during trial campaigns.
Several of these tracks have more than one hard filter, not just one entrance exam.
Entry into GSI and ONGC as a geologist runs through a competitive recruitment or GATE-linked exam and interview.
Clearing the Wildlife Institute of India's entrance test for its postgraduate programme is genuinely competitive on its own.

blocks.heading: Four Questions Before You Chase This

items.text: A pay table cannot tell you whether fieldwork-heavy science genuinely fits your temperament, your finances, and your life stage.

These careers reward people who can genuinely tolerate weeks away from home comforts, rough accommodation, physical exertion, and unpredictable schedules, and who do not treat fieldwork as a temporary adventure phase before "settling down" into a desk.

Fieldwork-heavy careers are genuinely harder to sustain around a young family, a caregiving responsibility, or a partner in a location-fixed job, since postings, cruises, and field seasons are rarely optional or fully schedulable around your life.

blocks.heading: Waste Years Chasing the Wrong Track

items.text: It is not one profession.
It is usually the lowest-paying and least stable of the six, mostly project-funded rather than permanent.
Entry-level science writing and reporting roles are mostly desk-based.

blocks.heading: Ranked By Travel and Ceiling
rows: Geology / mining & petroleum exploration
Field seasons at remote sites, drilling camps, or offshore rigs, a few weeks to months a year, mostly domestic
B.Sc/M.Sc Geology or Applied Geology, GATE for ONGC/PSU entry, or a state/GSI recruitment exam
Environmental / EIA fieldwork
Repeated short site visits for baseline sampling, project-by-project, almost entirely domestic
M.Sc Environmental Science, covered in depth in our environmental science careers guide
Marine biology & oceanography
Coastal fieldwork most of the year, occasional research-vessel cruises of a few weeks
M.Sc Marine Biology/Oceanography plus CSIR-UGC NET or a DBT/ICMR-JRF entrance route
Wildlife biology & conservation
Extended stretches living inside or near forests, reserves, and field stations
B.Sc/M.Sc Wildlife Science or Zoology, often with a WII or NGO fellowship as the real entry door
Science journalism & communication
Assignment-based: a launch, a conference, a field story, then back to a desk for weeks
Journalism/mass communication degree or a strong science-writing portfolio; no fixed entrance route
Polar/expedition and test-range science
The most dramatic on paper, and the rarest in practice: a handful of seats a year nationally
PhD-level specialisation (glaciology, atmospheric science) or a DRDO/ISRO scientist-entry exam

blocks.heading: Pay and How Much You Actually Travel
rows: Geology: junior exploration geologist, private mining/mineral company
Roughly Rs 4-7 LPA
Geology: ONGC/GSI geologist (post-GATE or recruitment exam)
Standard 7th CPC-linked PSU/government scale, rising steadily with seniority
Geology: senior consulting geologist, independent practice
Highly variable; meaningful upside usually after 8-10+ years of client relationships
Environmental/EIA fieldwork: junior associate
Roughly Rs 3-5 LPA (see the full environmental science pay table for every stage)
Marine biology/oceanography: JRF stage (CSIR-UGC NET/DBT-JRF)
Roughly Rs 37,000-42,000 a month fellowship, not a salary, capped at 5 years
Marine biology/oceanography: Scientist B, NIO/CMFRI (post-PhD or exam entry)
Roughly Rs 6-9 LPA entry, rising on a fixed government ladder

blocks.heading: Who Should Think Twice
rows: You are choosing between these fields mainly because "travel" sounds exciting

Travel here means remote camps, coastal field stations, forest postings, and short EIA site visits, not a scenic-photo career. Pick the underlying science first; the travel is a real but secondary feature of the job.
You are imagining polar expeditions or global assignments as a realistic entry-level outcome

NCPOR sends a handful of PhD-level scientists on Antarctic and Arctic missions a year. Nearly every geologist, marine biologist, wildlife researcher, and environmental scientist in India works entirely inside domestic postings.
You want a stable, predictable income and dislike project-to-project funding uncertainty

Wildlife and conservation fieldwork in particular runs on short-term, project-based funding for long stretches of a career. Government research posts are more stable, but the ladder to reach them is slow and exam-gated.
You are in, or planning, a family situation that needs consistent physical presence

Extended field seasons, research cruises, and remote postings genuinely strain relationships and parenting in ways worth discussing honestly with a partner or family before committing years of study to one of these tracks.

items.text: A field season of a few weeks to a few months at a remote site, camp, or field station, mostly within India.
Repeated short trips to a project site for sampling, surveying, or assessment, then weeks back at a desk.
An occasional research cruise, expedition, or assignment, genuinely exciting, but infrequent, not year-round.
